_note:
THE FIXTURE PACK: declarations, not cases (`cases` is empty on purpose and this file drives nothing). Every case in `g2p/` names a pack from here by id, and a malformed case names one plus a mutation recipe. THE PACK IS A DESCRIPTION OF BYTES, NEVER BYTES: a runner builds a real `.dspg` from this declaration (the layout is g2p-pack.md, 'The file'), applies the case's mutations, writes it somewhere, and loads it as an ordinary catalog entry, `{ "id": "fixture-en-1", "engine": "g2p", "format": "dspg", "path": "<built file>" }`. The corpus therefore ships no binary, stays diffable, and a mutation reads as one line of English instead of a hex blob.

THE PHONE ALPHABET IS DELIBERATELY NOT IPA. The PHON lines are `p0` through `p9` plus `pA` and `pB`, so nothing here can be mistaken for a pronunciation reference and no expectation in this corpus can be a guess about English. They are two characters wide on purpose: the wire renders a pronunciation by CONCATENATING phone names with no separator, so a fixed width keeps every expected string unambiguous. A pack declares phone SEQUENCES as id arrays because that is what the file holds; expectations quote the rendered string because that is what the envelope carries.

THE PACK CARRIES NO NORM SECTION, which is itself a fixture: number words are OPTIONAL, so a digit must still come back as a token (spelled) rather than vanish, 'absent, not wrong'. Real-pack accuracy is not a fixture question either: it is measured on a held-out split by the offline trainer and recorded in a shipped pack's own META, the same way real-model inference lives in the nightly smoke lane rather than in `ai/`.

fixture-en-1._note: The one base pack. Small enough to read, complete enough to load: META declares an `accept` set, SPEL names every code point in it (L3's proof), PHON has exactly `phone_count` lines, the lexicon carries plain entries plus one heteronym plus one plural that is its OWN entry (so the lexicon-beats-stem order is testable), the morphology rules carry two allomorphs (so a derivation is a rule and not a suffix), and the LTS trees are valid, with every child index strictly greater than its own node and one leaf emitting ZERO phones because a silent letter is correct rather than a dropped output.

meta.name: Corpus fixture (not a language)
meta._note_boundaries: `separators`, `punctuation` and `sentence_end` are the pack's, not the engine's, and the fixture states all three rather than leaning on a default. A pack that declares no `punctuation` keeps a comma inside the word it follows, which is correct for a script that punctuates differently and wrong for this one. `sentence_end` is what makes `defer` granular.
meta._note_fold: `fold` runs before anything else. ASCII case folding is expressed HERE and nowhere else, because `accept` carries no uppercase: a pack that forgets a pair refuses that letter, which is exactly the kind of gap L3 exists to make loud. The receipt is unaffected: a token's `text` is the input's own bytes, BEFORE folding.
meta._note_morphology: Two rules, and the `-s` rule carries TWO allomorphs so a derivation is visibly a rule applied to a dictionary fact rather than a suffix glued on. `after` names the stem's last phone: `walk` ends in `p3` and takes `p6`, `build` ends in `p9` and takes `pA`. The `-ed` rule undoubles, which is what lets `shipped` reach `ship`. Every derived pronunciation in this corpus is therefore computable from these rows plus the lexicon, so the stem cases pin exact strings rather than recording them.

fixture-en-1._note_phon: PHON: one phone per line, phone id IS the line index. Twelve lines, and META.phone_count says twelve. An integer here instead of a list means 'generate this many', which one validation case needs and nothing else uses.
fixture-en-1._note_lexicon: LEXK/LEXI/LEXV as one map. `form` 0 is one pronunciation; `form` 1 is POS-conditioned and its `senses` carry `pos` indices into META.pos_tags, where 0 is DEFAULT and must come first. `runs` is a lexicon entry in its own right even though `run` is one too. That is what makes 'lexicon before stem' a testable order rather than a claim. `builds`, `walks`, `walked` and `shipped` deliberately are NOT entries, so they must arrive via stem.
fixture-en-1._note_lts: `LTS `. `chr` is a LETTER ID (an index into META.letters), `pos` runs 0 to 2 × window with `window` itself being the letter being pronounced, and an out-of-range position answers with the padding id `letter_count`. Node 4 is a leaf of length ZERO, the silent letter, which is correct output and not a dropped one. Every child index here is strictly greater than its own node index; that is the property the infinite-walk guard checks and the property `validation.json` mutates. `roots` maps a letter to its starting node, and `*` is the root for every letter not named.
fixture-en-1._note_spel: SPEL, and L3's whole point: one row per code point in META.accept, all 45 of them, or the pack does not load. The file stores them sorted by code point; the builder sorts, the declaration is a map so a mutation can name one row. The row for SPACE is also the JOINER the speller puts between characters, so a spelled word's rendered phonemes are the rows for its characters interleaved with `p1`. That is what makes `spelled` expectations in this corpus concrete rather than recorded.
